title: Cartwise Shopper Batches Shown-Pay Shortfall Disputes and the Shopper's Pay-Dispute Filing Tool
content:
A shopper who holds that a completed batch of Cartwise Shopper Batches paid less than its accepted offer showed disputes it herself by submitting a shown-pay shortfall dispute on that batch, and the amount she claims on it is the claimed shortfall.

## When the claimed shortfall is settled

The claimed shortfall is fixed only after the batch's earnings entries carry a long-distance bonus whenever the estimated route exceeds the long-distance threshold that applies to the shopper.

The claimed shortfall is not worked out until every mileage posting that stands twice on the batch carries a reversal against its later posting.

Put the other way round: while the estimated route of the batch exceeds the long-distance threshold that applies to the shopper and its earnings entries carry no long-distance bonus, the claimed shortfall is not yet fixed; and while a mileage posting stands twice on the batch with no reversal against the later of the two, the claimed shortfall is not yet worked out.

## Who files the dispute

The dispute is the shopper's own filing, made on her own completed batch with the reason shown-pay shortfall and the claimed shortfall as the amount claimed.

## Situation of use and capability of `submit_pay_dispute_0c2b2ed2`

`submit_pay_dispute_0c2b2ed2` lets the shopper submit a pay dispute on one of her own shopper batches. One call files a single dispute on the named batch with the reason and the amount the shopper claims, stamped with the current time and standing as submitted; the shopper sees the new dispute and its reference number among her pay disputes at once.

## How it is invoked

It is the shopper's own tool: the agent unlocks `submit_pay_dispute_0c2b2ed2` and hands it over, and the customer themselves — here the shopper — runs it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `batch_id` | The batch number of the shopper's own batch being disputed, as read out to the shopper from the batch lookup | Id |
| `dispute_reason` | What the shopper says is missing | Enum, exactly one value from the list below |
| `claimed_amount_usd` | The amount the shopper claims is owed, in USD | A positive number with 2 decimal places; stored rounded to 2 decimal places |

Values of `dispute_reason`:

- `shown_pay_shortfall` — the batch paid less before tips than its accepted offer showed
- `mileage_underpaid` — the miles driven exceeded the estimated route beyond the tolerance and mileage pay fell short
- `heavy_pay_missing` — heavy pay for the batch's heavy units was not paid
- `wait_pay_missing` — waiting-time pay for recorded waiting was not paid
- `boost_missing` — the boost shown on the offer was not paid
- `cancellation_pay_missing` — the pay owed for a batch canceled after shopping started was not paid
- `return_pay_missing` — the pay for an order returned to the store was not paid

## Return

A text receipt of a dictionary carrying `batch_pay_dispute_id` (the reference number of the new dispute), `batch_id`, `dispute_reason`, `claimed_amount_usd` (USD, 2 decimal places), `dispute_status` (always submitted) and `created_at` (the submission time, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS). Receiving the `batch_pay_dispute_id` means the dispute is filed.
